changesSinceB4: B5 preserves a valid semantic-eligible comparison across later ineligible comparison alternatives. Ordinary hard-fact rejections still cannot use that path.
B5 adds one generic counted-request-introduction sentence to Light, plus native policy cues so these clear requests are not skipped before the model. Full and verifier prompt files remain unchanged.

B6 recognizes a retained One more thing phrase independent of punctuation. Only the optional marker-removed comparison also requires each ordered normalized number and its next two content tokens to match, so a retained or reworded discourse one cannot replace a dropped one backup. This is a hard check before semantic eligibility.
All other literal, language, quantity, duration, currency, negation, ending and cancellation protections remain in effect.
limits: These are offline synthetic checks with injected responses and an independent local guard audit. They test safety/routing, not model correctness. The full provider study ran on B5; three focused provider cases ran on B6. No microphone or native insertion claim.
